source.title: SCOUT: Sim-to-Real Text-Based Person Retrieval by Embedding-Space Prediction over Frozen Video Features
source.authors: Abdarahmane Traoré; Andy Couturier; Éric Hervet

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some embedded figures are garbled, but the relevant alignment results are also stated in text and Table 2.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether alignment measures predict retrieval across frozen text targets and reports that the relationship changes by metric when a fourth target is added, including an inverted ridge-probe correlation.
record.gate_note: The study measures alignment between frozen video and text representations and compares those measurements with retrieval results. Other training ablations and leaderboard results do not measure representation alignment and are not included. The study does not sweep model scale or capability.
record.test_reason: The study measures alignment between frozen V-JEPA video features and four frozen text encoders on paired val data with three metrics (mutual kNN, linear CKA, ridge R2). The metrics rank the targets differently once Qwen3-Emb is added, which bears on V6. The ridge R2 values directly measure how well a linear map carries video features onto text embeddings, which bears on V4. The correlations of alignment with SCOUT retrieval, and the retrieval scores themselves, concern the study's own method and are a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present alignment-based target selection as a training-free screening heuristic, not a validated law. It holds within a family of comparable encoders, while the LLM-based Qwen3-Emb target breaks it unevenly across metrics, with mutual kNN the most robust lens. They attribute the failure to the learned mapping rather than the target's static geometry. They also note the evidence covers one encoder family and one benchmark that was also used for selection, so it is not an untouched holdout.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mutual-kNN overlap, CKA, and ridge-probe alignment to screen text targets and relate them to retrieval; it does not reproduce a representation-convergence-with-scale experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The metric changes the alignment-to-retrieval relationship after adding Qwen3-Embedding: kNN ρ = 0.8, CKA ρ = 0.4, and ridge R2 ρ = −0.2. Within the first three targets, all three metrics give the same ordering.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-free alignment between V-JEPA and each text target orders the targets identically to the retrieval of SCOUT trained on them (rho=1.0, n=3). With Qwen3-Emb added, kNN rho=0.8, CKA 0.4, ridge R2 −0.2 (n=4, p≥0.2). The authors attribute the failure to the learned mapping, not the static geometry; correcting for anisotropy did not repair the ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model representational alignment predicts how well a downstream predictor trained to map into one model's space will perform, and this predictiveness depends on the alignment metric.

record.problems: The alignment comparison uses one held-out synthetic validation split and a small number of candidate text encoders. Correlation estimates use n = 3 or n = 4 and the paper reports p ≥ 0.2 for the four-target correlations. The authors say the criterion is a heuristic, not a validated law.
record.rows_left_out: No other alignment-measure results bearing on the claim were reported. The remaining ablations and leaderboard results concern retrieval performance or system components, not representation alignment.

untested.parts: No sweep of model scale or capability across independently trained models.

Video-text alignment on paired data is measured, but there is no test of whether it rises as the models improve. Text encoder size does not order alignment (CLIP-text 123M aligns more than EmbeddingGemma 300M), but capability is not measured.
No stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping. Only the ridge linear probe is used.
No interpretable features or circuits are examined.
No variation of k for mutual kNN, of the input distribution, or of out-of-distribution data for the alignment scores themselves. Only one synthetic val split is used.

No ceiling or baseline is given for the alignment scores, and plateau is not tested. Shared data or objectives as the cause is only argued informally: CLIP-text's image-text training is suggested to explain its higher alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The record treated alignment-to-retrieval correlations as V6 evidence. Those concern the predictiveness of the study's own method, so V6 is now judged from the alignment values themselves, read across metrics. The alignment rows are per-target single values, so their states reflect the target's rank consistency across metrics. Raw kNN (about 0.2) and CKA (about 0.4–0.48) are on different scales and are not compared directly. The alignment comparisons rest on n=3–4 targets and a single video encoder.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep of independently trained models.
Although the study measures video-text alignment on paired data, it does not test whether alignment rises as both models improve.
No comparison across seeds of the same architecture.
No test of mapping one model's representations onto another's, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.

The study compares alignment metrics on one held-out synthetic validation split; it does not test other input distributions, neighbour-count settings, or whether the alignment measurements themselves change out of distribution.
The study does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain cross-model alignment, or measure whether alignment plateaus.
